heading: Pick a model by what you care about
mobileHint: Tap or drag the triangle to set your priorities.
mapDescription: A triangle of hexagons. Each corner stands for caring about only one thing: Smarter, Faster or Cheaper. Each hexagon is a different mix of those priorities, and its color shows the top model for that mix among the checked creators. The ring marks your current priorities and can sit between hexagons. Use the arrow keys to move between hexagons and Enter to pick one.
winnerNote: These are the model's measured values from the catalog. The triangle sets how much each one matters to you, not a target score, time or cost.
creatorsHint: Only models from checked creators can win a hexagon or appear in the table. Regret is still measured against the Full Catalog frontier, so unchecking a creator removes rivals without rescoring anyone. The search box below only filters the table.

captionEmpty: No frontier models · no creators checked
emptyCreators: No creators are checked, so there is no model to rank. Open Creators above and check at least one, or choose Select all.
whyIntro: Each number is a weighted regret: the model's gap from the best Full Catalog frontier value on that axis, divided by that frontier's interquartile range, then weighted by how much that axis matters in your current priorities. Regret has no units, and lower is better.
whyDerivedFrontier: This model belongs to the Full Catalog frontier on the considered axes. Its position follows Speedshop's precomputed ranking for these priorities: {priorities}. Creator filters only narrow that published ranking. Underlying source measurements and numeric ranking scores are not published.
derivedNonEndorsement: The visualization and rankings were created by Speedshop and do not represent the views or endorsement of {provider}.
whyScore: Worst regret {value}. The largest weighted regret is the limiting trade-off: it sets the rank, and ties go to the lower mean weighted regret.
whyScoreTied: Worst regret {value}, shared by {axes}. Together they are the limiting trade-off: they set the rank, and ties go to the lower mean weighted regret.
whyNoRegret: Worst regret {value}. Every considered axis adds zero weighted regret, so no trade-off limits this model's rank. Zero does not always mean the best value: when the Full Catalog frontier has only one distinct value on an axis, such as at a corner of the triangle, there is no spread to measure gaps against, and every model scores zero on that axis.

explainRanking: The page ranks models in two steps. First it keeps only models from the creators checked under Creators, then drops every one that another checked model matches or beats on every axis you consider and beats on at least one of them. The models left over form the Pareto frontier. An axis is not considered when your priorities sit on the triangle's edge opposite its corner, and it then plays no part in this step or the next.
Then it sorts the frontier by interquartile minimax regret, weighting each axis by how much it matters in your priorities. The model whose worst case is least bad comes first.

Each hexagon is one mix of priorities: the closer it sits to a corner, the more that corner matters. Its color is the model that ranks first for that mix. Click or tap a hexagon to use its mix, or drag across the triangle, or drag the ring itself, to fine-tune your priorities. The ring marks your current priorities, which can sit between hexagons. A spot on the triangle is a mix of priorities, not a target score, time or cost.

Colors group models by creator. Each major creator has its own hue, and each of its model families gets a nearby shade of that hue. Within one family, a higher thinking level is always darker, and a variant without a recognized thinking level gets the family's middle shade. Smaller creators can share a hue with each other.

Beneath the triangle, the top model for your current priorities is shown with its actual Smart, Time and Cost values from the catalog. The table lists the whole frontier for your current priorities. The search box only narrows the table: it never changes the triangle or the ranking.
explainRegret: For each axis, a model's regret is how far it sits from the best value on the Full Catalog frontier: the frontier of every model in the catalog, whichever creators are checked. That gap is divided by the interquartile range of the axis across that frontier, so a gap counts as big or small relative to how spread out the frontier is. Time uses a log scale, so halving the time counts the same whether a task takes ten seconds or ten minutes. Because this yardstick never changes with your creator choice, unchecking a creator removes rivals but leaves every other model's regret the same.

Each axis's regret is then weighted by how much that axis matters in your priorities. A model's score is its largest weighted regret, and ties go to the lower mean weighted regret. The lowest score wins. Regret has no units, and lower is better. Open Why this model? on any row to see its weighted regret on each axis.
Put simply, the top model is the one that is never far behind on anything you care about.
explainMetricsTitle: How Smart, Time and Cost are measured
explainMetricsIntro: Every number comes straight from the catalog, with no adjustment by this page.
explainData: This page uses {name}, version {version}, generated on {date}.
explainEmbedded: The page carries a stripped copy of the catalog: each model's name, creator, thinking level, release date and three metrics. It makes no network requests, so it works offline and sends nothing anywhere. Rebuild the page to pick up new data.
footerMethod: Pareto frontier over the axes you consider, then interquartile minimax regret.
